title: ZCC web privacy (User Privacy) calls: string flags, fields the contract lacks, and key casing

prose.text: Web privacy is one tenant-wide settings object, read with `getWebPrivacyInfo` and written with `setWebPrivacyInfo`. {{single-object}} What the individual settings do is in [[zcc.web-privacy.collection]].

prose.label: Fields beyond the contract.
prose.text: {{contract-lacks-three}} {{python-model-lacks-three}} The Python read returns a dictionary rather than the model: [[zcc.sdk-python.return-shapes:web-privacy-get-dict]]. {{fqdn-key-casing}}

prose.label: Writes.
prose.text: {{go-update-rereads}} The Python write sends any keyword it is given: [[zcc.sdk-python.return-shapes:python-set-kwargs]]. How the provider fills two of these fields from state, and why its data source reports them false, is in [[zcc.terraform.field-fidelity:prior-state-overlays-elsewhere]] and [[zcc.terraform.field-fidelity:data-sources-report-false-for-dropped-fields]].

checks.do: Whether a hand-built body sent the toggles as the strings "1" and "0" rather than JSON booleans.
Whether a Python write of the FQDN match setting used the snake_case keyword, which goes out under a different casing from the Go SDK's key.
When a setting reads back off, check whether the key is one the contract omits and the client fills from elsewhere.

provider-sends-01.statement: The Terraform provider writes each web privacy toggle as "1" or "0" and reads it back as true only when the value is "1", except `enforceSecurePacUrls` and `enableFQDNMatchForVpnBypasses`, whose read-back keeps the prior plan or state value when one is set; the Python docstring example passes the same strings.
provider-sends-01.conditions: Extended per verifier with the two fields the provider fills from prior state (zcc.terraform.field-fidelity:prior-state-overlays-elsewhere).

contract-lacks-three.statement: The Go web privacy type also carries `enableAutoLogSnippet`, `enforceSecurePacUrls` and `enableFQDNMatchForVpnBypasses`, none of which the contract's get or set schema lists.
contract-lacks-three.conditions: Absence in the contract: both schemas list `active`, `collectMachineHostname`, `collectUserInfo`, `collectZdxLocation`, `disableCrashlytics`, `enablePacketCapture`, `exportLogsForNonAdmin`, `grantAccessToZscalerLogFolder`, `id`, `overrideT2ProtocolSetting` and `restrictRemotePacketCapture` only.

python-model-lacks-three.statement: The Python `WebPrivacy` model reads none of the three, so `set_web_privacy_info`, which returns that model, drops them from its result even when the caller sent them.
python-model-lacks-three.conditions: Absence: models/webprivacy.py has no key for the three fields.

single-object.statement: Web privacy is a single settings record, not a list: the API document's GET takes no parameters and returns an object, the Go SDK returns a single struct, and the Terraform provider documents it as a singleton.

Manages the singleton ZCC web privacy settings (logging, packet capture, and information-collection toggles).

fqdn-key-casing.statement: The Go SDK sends the FQDN-match-for-VPN-bypasses setting as `enableFQDNMatchForVpnBypasses`, but a Python caller who passes the snake_case keyword `enable_fqdn_match_for_vpn_bypasses` sends `enableFqdnMatchForVpnBypasses`, because the Python converter camel-cases word by word and has no exception for this key. A Python caller can pass the Go spelling as the keyword instead, since a key without an underscore is sent as given; the contract omits the field, so which spelling the API reads is not shown.
fqdn-key-casing.conditions: Changed per verifier from a divergence to a claim: no Python source names the field, so the Python spelling is computed, not a stated position. Traced through `to_lower_camel_case` (zscaler/helpers.py, no FIELD_EXCEPTIONS entry for the key); not run.
